title: Org Structure (Departments & People)
markdown:
The org model has two persistent registries backed by SQLite (both share `episodic_memory.db`): **departments** and **people**. Eight default departments are seeded exactly once per database on first boot, tracked by a `default_departments_seeded` sentinel in `departments_meta`; after that the user owns the list and deleted departments stay deleted across restarts.

### Company setup (onboarding)
Both registries are first populated by **conversational onboarding** at
`/onboard`. The user describes their business in their own words (optionally
attaching a deck or one-pager); the `onboarding_interviewer` agent — Council-
visible but outside `SPECIALIST_REGISTRY`, so the Executive cannot reach it via
`consult_specialist` — asks up to 8 clarifying questions, then emits a draft
company profile, a leadership roster, and a department list. The user reviews
and edits that draft inline (the same section editors `/company-profile` uses)
before anything is written.

Two properties matter here. First, **the interview never writes**: the whole
exchange lives in an in-memory, TTL'd session, and the single write happens at
`POST /onboard/interview/commit`, so a rejected save leaves the draft editable
and retryable. Second, **the department step is additive** — drafted
departments are matched onto existing ones by slug or title and updated in
place, unmatched ones are created, and nothing is ever deleted. That is
deliberately unlike the fixture loader's `_seed_departments`, which DELETEs
every row first: doing that here would drop the eight defaults along with their
`specialist_key` wiring, which `create_department` (always `specialist_key =
NULL`) cannot restore. `profile.org_structure` is derived from the reviewed
people and department tables at commit time, so it cannot drift from them.

Exactly one person is marked `is_principal` and receives `WILDCARD` authority;
no contact details are imported, even if the user volunteers them, because
channels and handles are a deliberate action on the People page. The one
exception is the owner's own sign-in email: the review screen has a separate
field for it, pre-filled with the current owner's email on a re-run and with the
signed-in user's on a first setup. The commit checks it before writing anything
(malformed, already another person's, or different from the owner's existing
email is a 422 — setup only fills in a missing one) and then saves it on the
principal's row. Without it the signed-in owner matched no Person,
so their chat history stayed empty until they found the People page. With
local login (`make dev` without Google sign-in) the field is optional: that
session carries no email, which the backend already reads as the principal.
Because the save demotes the old principal, only the current owner may draft
someone else as "This is me" when setup is re-run (403 otherwise); a re-run
that keeps the owner, or a first setup, is open to anyone who can sign in. The original
12-step form wizard remains available at `/onboard?mode=form` and backs the
`openexecutive onboard` CLI.

A first setup opens on one question — **Just me** or **Me and my team** — and
the choice is written to `PUT /workspace` (with the browser's time zone) before
the conversation starts, because the two modes ask different things. A re-run
over an existing profile skips it; the mode is changed in Settings. In solo the
interviewer's first user turn carries a short hint (the founder runs the
business alone: draft only them, as principal, and no departments; ask about
the offer, customers, pricing, cash and runway and their top goals instead of
a leadership team). It rides in the user turn, so the cached system prompt is
the same constant in both modes. The solo review screen shows only **You**
(name and role) and the sign-in email, and commits that one principal with no
departments — the existing departments stay, as the areas goals are grouped
by. The form wizard (and the CLI) read the mode when a session starts and skip
the Team Size, Team Members and Fractional Executives steps in solo; each
status response numbers the steps it actually asks and flags whether the
current one is `optional`.

### Departments
Each department carries a charter, `Goal` rows, `ChecklistItem`s, and named cadences. Cadence specs (`daily@HH:MM`, `weekly@DOW@HH:MM`, `quarterly@DD-HH:MM`, UTC) run a `department_check_in` workflow when due (never in solo mode, below), then chain the next occurrence; `PATCH /departments/{slug}` rejects a spec that does not parse with a 422. The check-in is skipped (and still chained) when the department has no specialist, no Goals, or nothing new since its Goals were last reviewed. An idle initiative is chased with the department's head, or with the principal when there is none. A department may map to a specialist agent via `specialist_key`, or stay informational. No department is seeded for the `sales` specialist (existing installs keep their departments unchanged), so its consults skip the department-memory prefetch and the Honcho department sync, as `triage`'s do. An assigned head gets a generated department-head voice persona.

A department can also list **watched entities** (`watched_entities`, edited one per line on its page): vendors it is evaluating, competitors in its lane, tickers it tracks. The research watch policy treats them as strong grounding — a proposal about one can be added to the watch list on its own — and routes the resulting watch, its alerts and any suggestion cards to the department and its head rather than the principal (see External monitoring).

### Solo and team mode
An install is either a **team** (the default) or **solo** — one person using Open Executive just for themselves. The mode lives with the user's time zone in its own one-row table, `workspace_settings` (`openexecutive.memory.workspace_settings`, `GET`/`PUT /workspace`), not on the company profile, because onboarding's commit and the form wizard rebuild the profile from scratch and would wipe it. Changing it is the principal's call (open while no principal exists, so first-run setup can choose).

Solo turns the department rhythm off without touching the org: switching to solo cancels every pending `dept_cadence` row, `bootstrap_cadences` does nothing (the check sits inside it, so boot, the fixture reset and client-slot activation all honour it), and the scheduler cancels any stray check-in without running or chaining it, and a check-in already running across the switch schedules no successor. Department and people rows are kept, so switching back to team re-schedules the check-ins at once. The boot-time org-completeness warnings (departments with no head) are skipped in solo. A chat `Session` can carry an explicit `workspace_mode` override (read through `effective_workspace_mode`), so a caller that runs many conversations on one Executive — evals, for one — can pick the mode per session instead of flipping the install-wide setting.

In the UI, a `WorkspaceProvider` in the root layout reads the mode once (and again after Settings changes it) and reads **team** while loading or on error, so a team install never flashes the solo UI. Solo swaps the sidebar's Company group for **You** — Goals, People, Business profile — where `/goals` lists every goal grouped by area (a department row) and adds, edits and deletes them through the slug-scoped goal routes. `/departments` and `/people` stay reachable by URL.

The setting is per company: a blank client slot starts on the defaults, a saved slot keeps its own, a fixture load resets it and applies the fixture's optional `workspace.yaml` (read and validated before anything is swapped; a bad value is skipped, never a failed load), and the factory reset returns it to team with no zone. The user's own settings survive a demo: the backup a fixture load takes (or reuses) always gets the live settings written to its `workspace.yaml` while the live state is the user's, and an unload from an older backup without one leaves the settings as they are. A zone that cannot be loaded is never fatal — the API answers 422, and a stored one reads as unset.

### Authority gate
Each department declares an `AuthorityLevel`, which `departments.authority.gate_action` checks whenever a department-scoped scheduled action comes due. The check-in cadence is the exception: it sends nothing itself, and each action it proposes is run through the gate and shown with its verdict in the report — so a propose-only department's check-ins actually run instead of becoming a one-shot approval card. `auto_execute` (autonomous) fires directly. `propose_only` turns the action into an approval card for an approver (`propose_via_alert`) and sends nothing, deferring the card to the approver's next availability window when they are outside it. `escalate` also sends nothing until someone approves: it raises an urgent `[ESCALATION]` card (severity high) right away, never deferred — filed unrouted when nobody holds the scope and no principal is set, since the Briefing lists every unread card — what the Departments page promises ("the specialist will not act — it forwards everything to a human"). It used to raise the card *and* dispatch, so approving the card sent the action a second time. Calendar bookings follow the same rule. The approver is chosen by `AuthorityScope` — a scheduled action's `required_scope` (e.g. `vendor_onboarding`, `spend_lt_10k`) feeds `find_approvers(scope)`, which ranks non-principal scope-holders ahead of `WILDCARD` holders. A null/unknown scope falls back to `WILDCARD` (the principal).

### People & channels
The people registry resolves each `Person` to a `(channel, channel_ref)` pair via `prefer_channel_for()`, honoring `preferred_channel` (falling back email → slack → discord → telegram) and availability windows. The principal briefs use their own order — the preferred channel, then Slack → Discord → Telegram, with email only for an `email` preference or an `any` principal with no chat channel (see Scheduler). Departments can also set `slack_channel_id` / `discord_channel_id` / `telegram_chat_id` to broadcast to a team room instead of DMing the head.

Each person's page also lists their **open loops** (see Attunement) — what they committed to or were asked for in conversation — with a *Mark done* action; archiving a person closes their open loops, since an archived person can no longer be chased. The list is the principal's or that person's only; `people.store.is_principal_or_self` is the one check behind it, the close action and reply feedback.

The Executive can change the roster from a chat turn (`upsert_person`, `archive_person`, `set_department_head`) only when the principal asks, from the web chat, their own Slack or Discord, or a private Telegram chat when `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is set to a value Telegram can send. A teammate, an email (even one from the principal's address), Google Chat, the CLI, the MCP server and unattended runs are refused, because a team member's People row is also the web sign-in allow-list, the outbound-email allow-list and approval routing. The People page itself is unaffected.

### Team and contacts
A `Person` is either on the **team** (`kind = "team"`, the default) or a **contact** (`kind = "contact"`): a client, contractor or advisor the Executive may need to email or invite but who must not get what a team row grants. Before contacts existed, emailing a client meant adding them as a Person, which also let them sign in and talk to the bot.

Contacts are **denied by default**. `people.store.list_people`, every `find_person_by_*` (and `find_person_by_channel_ref`), and the `people.registry` cache return team members only unless the caller passes `include_contacts=True`; `find_approvers` has no opt-in at all. So a contact is never in the web sign-in list (`GET /auth/allowed-emails`), the Slack / Telegram / Discord inbound gates, approvers, the alert review's roster slice, `/today`'s people list and insights, open-loop owners (an ask of a contact opens no loop, so the nudge engine never chases them), a workflow gate's approver or cadence recipient, the recap DM after a meeting, or a department head (`set_department_head` and `PATCH /departments/{slug}` refuse one). `get_person(id)` returns either kind and its security-relevant callers check `kind`.

The roster reads that **opt in** are few: the Executive's egress checks (Gmail, Calendar and Drive in the MCP gateway, calendar attendee resolution, and the chat DM tools), the People page's listing (`GET /people?include_contacts=true`), the chat `list_people` tool (both kinds, with `kind`), and the org prompt block. Even there, reaching a contact needs **the principal's own turn**: `people_tools.contacts_reachable_now()` is true only on a turn the principal started on a surface that verified them — the same rule as roster writes above — or inside `grant_contact_egress()`, which the decisions approve route uses when the approver resolves to the principal. An inbound email (even from the principal's address), a teammate's turn, and unattended runs (scheduler, workflows, alert review) can still reach the team but not contacts. A workflow resumed by `apply_resolution`'s kick runs with no chat session, like the resumer's poll loop, so it never inherits the approver's turn.

**Contacts are private to the principal.** A solo user may be an executive whose contacts include their boss, reports, board and clients, so nobody else using the install sees one. The rule is `contacts_reachable_now()` again: off the principal's own verified turn a contact does not exist — `list_people` returns the team with the same count, a contact's id or address gets exactly the error an unknown one gets (never a contact-specific refusal), and the org prompt block has no Contacts section. The API applies the same rule by caller (`people.caller_is_principal`: the signed-in email is the principal's, or no `x-caller-email` — CLI, local login): `?include_contacts=true` is ignored for anyone else, a contact's id is a 404 on every `/people/{id}` route exactly like a missing one, only the principal may create a contact or turn someone into one (403), and `GET /people/me` tells the UI whether to offer contacts at all.

Whatever the Executive raises about a contact stays with the principal too. A meeting with a contact is proposed to the principal (not the scope's approver), its decision is hidden from everyone else's `/decisions` (404 by id), and its card carries `alerts.models.PRIVATE_ALERT_TAG`. So does an alert raised on a turn about the principal's private mail (`Session.private_to_principal`, set by the email poller for mail from a contact and for mail the principal forwards): the pipeline routes it to the principal, stores it without a live push or broadcast, and dedups it only against other private alerts. Private alerts appear on the principal's own `/today` and chat digest only — never a teammate's, the activity rail, the narrative, the morning brief, the end-of-day digest, the reflection or the alert review — and a teammate's ack, reopen or bulk sweep cannot touch one (404). A private turn itself reaches the principal and nobody else (email, DMs, invites) and cannot publish an artifact, which the whole team can see. DMs to a contact stay off the activity rail.

`upsert_person` takes `kind`: explicit wins; an update that omits it keeps the row's kind (the store's full-row UPDATE preserves it, so nothing promotes a contact to the team by accident); a new person defaults to `team`, or to `contact` in solo mode. On the principal's own verified turn the org prompt block lists contacts in a short `## Contacts` section after the team section — name, role/company and whether an email is on file, capped at 25 — in both modes. Every other turn gets the team block, byte-identical to an install with no contacts, so the 5-minute cached block has two stable variants.

On the **People page** the principal sees **Team** and **Contacts** tabs; anyone else sees the team only (no Contacts tab, no kind selector). Solo mode opens on Contacts, and its Team tab shows only the principal. The add form has a kind selector and hides authority scopes, reply SLA and the principal checkbox for a contact; a contact's page hides scopes, SLA, availability windows, open loops, outreach and working style. Adding a team member in solo offers to switch the workspace to team mode, or keep solo.
mermaid:
flowchart TD
  People["People registry (Person, is_principal, kind)"]
  Contacts["Contacts (kind = contact): egress only on the principal's turn"]
  Dept["Departments (8 seeded once)"]
  GC["Goals / checklists / cadences"]
  Head["Head + voice persona"]
  Gate["Authority gate (propose_only vs autonomous)"]
  Scope["AuthorityScope to find_approvers"]
  Chan["Channel resolution (Discord / Telegram / email)"]
  Dept --> GC
  Dept --> Head
  Dept -->|proposes action| Gate
  Gate -->|required_scope| Scope
  Scope -->|ranks approvers| People
  People --> Chan
  People -. include_contacts .-> Contacts
  Dept -->|team room| Chan
  class People storage
  class Contacts storage
  class Dept storage
  class GC storage
  class Gate compute
  class Scope compute
  class Chan compute
  class Head compute
